content: Currently new members is used for both introductions and for "easy" questions. What if we split it up into two channels: #introductions and #beginner questions?

Given #42901 and website#907, I think the trend is to do to opposite :)
That said, I do agree that easy questions from non-beginners don't have a home. You could then still use #new members but it's a bit weird, so you can use #general (or #mathlib4 if it's mathlib related).

#basic questions maybe? I've asked some questions there in the past because they were elementary questions about topics not in my area of expertise (eg type theory or parts of mathlib which I don't usually inhabit)
Rename to #getting started maybe? It could mean both someone getting started or getting started on something (not familiar with), just as its current dual use.

On discord servers, there is usually a #getting-started for how what to do. Not sure if Zulip supports such a feature, but that would maybe prevent some of the post asking for edit permissions and people asking questions in #new members. Renaming #new members to that would feel weird to me considering how its used on other platforms, i.e. as purely read only info. I do like the #introductions name suggestion.

I am a little confused about why #mathlib4 would not also be the right place for asking easy questions for non-beginners. Seems to work reasonably well to me.
